messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · INC-2026-042 · SEV2
• Summary: elevated p95/p99 latency on generation APIs in us-west-2 (affects all small->large models)
• Pager: @mike
• Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inc-2026-042

mike: taking pager. starting quick triage — looking at autoscaler and recent kernel rollout. will post initial impact in 5.

amy: TY. Communications here — we should draft a short status page blurb + one customer-facing email. Also want a tweet-ready line if we need to post to socials.

laura: support intake: a handful of enterprise tenants reported degraded generation times ~2:30a PT. Not seeing errors, just slow responses. No data exfil reports.

sam: mitigation in progress: rolling back the kernel selection change from earlier today to the previous golden build on a small canary. If that fails, fallback to model-variant routing (lower-capacity variant) for latency-sensitive customers.

dan: current metrics: p95 latency 1.9s -> 4.8s, p99 3.4s -> 12.2s, error rate steady at ~0.1%. Token throughput down ~30%.

amy: status page draft (SHORT — for immediate publish):

-----BEGIN STATUS BLURB-----
We are investigating elevated latencies for the Redwood generation API in the US-West region. A subset of requests may experience slower response times; generation accuracy is unaffected. Our on-call team is actively mitigating and we will update this page with new information and ETA.
Affected region: US-West
Customer impact: increased response times for generation requests (partial degradation)
Next update: in 15 minutes or when we have an ETA.
-----END STATUS BLURB-----

amy: customer email sketch (for tenants with SLA concerns):

-----BEGIN CUSTOMER EMAIL-----
Subject: Temporary increased latency on Redwood generation API (US-West)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re investigating an issue causing increased latency for generation requests in our US-West region. Our teams are actively working on mitigation; accuracy of outputs is not affected. We’ll share an update within 30 minutes and follow up with a root cause and timeline once available.

If you need immediate assistance or mitigation (e.g., failover to another region / dedicated capacity), reply and we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Redwood Support
-----END CUSTOMER EMAIL-----

kate-pr: thanks. For any public social post we need sign-off from @kate-pr (comms) + @legal (if we name specific customers). Keep tweet non-identifying and aligned with status page.

mike: quick technical note for status page/ops log to explain mitigation steps (can paste as internal note):

```
Mitigation steps executed:
1) Rolled back inference kernel build 2026-04-10-09 to 2026-04-09-18 on canary nodes (us-west-2a).
2) Observed p95 drop from 4.8s -> 2.1s on canary within 6m.
3) Gradual rollout to remaining nodes under 5m windows; watching cache warm and KV hit-rate.
4) If regression observed, will route latency-sensitive traffic to quantized model-variant vq-1.
```

laura: for internal comms, please add an explicit line: "No PII or SSO errors observed. Investigating kernel selection and scheduling pressure."

amy: two tweet options — please pick one (short + aligned with status page):

1) "We're investigating increased latency for the Redwood generation API in US‑West. Our teams are working on a fix; accuracy unaffected. Status: https://status.redwood/INC-2026-042"

2) "Redwood: experiencing higher response times in US‑West for generation APIs. Mitigation underway; updates on status.redwood.com."

kate-pr: pref 1 for clarity (link to status). I'll get legal if we need to name anything more.

sam: operational ask: can comms hold public post until canary shows stable p95 < 2.5s for 10m? Otherwise we'll post the status page only.

amy: agreed. We'll prepare the tweet but will not post until ops confirms canary stability. Comms will publish the status page immediately (short).

dan: adding note for incident timeline:
• 02:30 PT — latency spike start
• 02:33 PT — pager fired to @mike
• 02:36 PT — rolled back kernel on canary
• 02:42 PT — canary p95 improved to 2.1s
• 02:48 PT — started gradual rollout

mike: action items (live):
- @sam continue rollout and monitor p95/p99 + KV hit-rate (ETA next update 10m)
- @amy publish the short status page blurb now
- @laura prepare customer email template to send to any tenants who ask (do not send proactively without exec sign-off)
- @kate-pr standby for tweet sign-off once canary stable
- @dan capture metrics and add to incident timeline

amy: published status page (link: https://status.redwood/INC-2026-042) — tagging here so agents know it's live.

laura: ack — creating a support queue note and copying the customer email template into escalations doc.

kate-pr: I'll ping legal now. If they give a green light, we'll post tweet option 1 once @sam confirms stability window.

sam: canary stable at 02:56 PT — p95 2.0s, p99 3.1s, KV hit-rate normal. continuing rollout. will update in 5.

mike: excellent. @kate-pr / @amy please go ahead with the social post (option 1) and signal ops when posted so we can close the loop.

amy: posted tweet at 03:02 PT: "We're investigating increased latency for the Redwood generation API in US‑West. Our teams are working on a fix; accuracy unaffected. Status: https://status.redwood/INC-2026-042" :white_check_mark:

kate-pr: legal gave verbal OK — no customer names. Good job everyone.

dan: adding final postmortem note: make sure to include kernel selection test matrix and canary gating for future rollouts (document: https://redwood/eng/reviews/inc-2026-042)

mike: incident moving to recovery. oncall handing off to daytime rotation at 04:00 PT — new pager: @dana (outside this thread). Closing this thread once all postmortem actions assigned.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED · INC-2026-042 · status changed to RECOVERY · primary reporter: mike

-- end of thread --
